full_judgment:
This Rule is directed against the order dated 1-1-96 passed by the District Judge, Thakurgaon in Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1995 under Order 47 rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, refusing to review his order dated 25-11-95 passed in Title Appeal No. 18 of 1995, arising out of the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 28 of 1991 by the Assistant Judge, Pirganj dismissing the suit on contest. 

 2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of the case are that, the petitioners as plaintiffs instituted a suit in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Pirganj in the District of Thakurgaon, being Other Class Suit No. 28 of 1991, praying for declaration of title in the suit land and for permanent injunction. 

 5. Mr. Marfat Ali, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the learned District Judge evidently erred in law in passing the impugned order without applying his judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and the law bearing on the subject and the same has occasioned failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that in view of the fact that the appellant petitioners never prayed for withdrawal of the appeal, learned District Judge evidently erred in law in ordering the withdrawal of the appeal on misapprehension of fact, with a cost of Taka 2500.00 to the respondents instead of allowing the plaintiff-appellants prayer for withdrawal of the suit on the ground of formal defects, with permission to sue afresh on the same subject matter. 

 7. The learned Advocate for the petitioners has placed before me the impugned order. He has also placed before me the application for withdrawal of the suit on setting aside the impugned decree passed by the learned trial Court, This application has been marked as Annexure 'C' to the petitioner. From this application it is evident that the plaintiff-petitioners prayed for withdrawal of the suit on the ground of formal defects on setting aside the impugned decree passed by the learned trial Court. There was no prayer for withdrawal of the appeal itself. The order of the learned District Judge dated 25-11-95 madein Title Appeal No. 17 of 1995 appears to be a bundle of confusion and the product of non-application of his judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and the application of the appellants. 

 10. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost and the impugned order dated 1-1-96 passed by the learned District Judge, Thakurgaon in Misc. Case No. 9 of 1995 is set aside. The learned District Judge, Thakurgaon is, hereby directed to rehear the petitioners' application dated 6-11-95 for withdrawal of the suit on the ground of formal defects with permission to sue afresh, on its own merit in accordance with law. 

 12. In view of the fact that this-is a very old case, the learned District Judge is directed to dispose of the petitioners' application dated 6-11-95 for withdrawal of the suit on the ground of formal defects with permission to sue afresh on the same cause of action within six weeks from the date of receipt of this order, with notice to the contending parties.
